name: Llama Guard 3-1B-INT4: Compact and Efficient Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
problem: LLM-based guardrails are a SECOND MODEL ON THE CRITICAL PATH of every conversation, so their size and latency are a direct tax on every interaction - and the 8B-class guard models are too heavy to deploy on constrained or edge devices.
mechanism: Two compounding changes to the same guardrail design as Llama Guard (pap-eff-llama-guard-safeguard-model): shrink the guard model to the 1B class AND quantise it to INT4, yielding a 440MB artifact. The int4 quantisation is what makes it run on a commodity ARM CPU at all - the deployment target is a phone-class device, not a datacenter GPU, so the entire cost argument is about fitting the guardrail on hardware that already exists at the edge.
speedup_reported: At least 30 TOKENS PER SECOND throughput and time-to-first-token of 2.5 SECONDS OR LESS ON A COMMODITY ANDROID MOBILE CPU. Attains COMPARABLE OR SUPERIOR safety moderation scores to its larger counterpart Llama Guard 3-1B, despite being approximately 7 TIMES SMALLER in size (440MB). This is one of the very few records in the entire set that quotes a concrete tok/s and TTFT for a deployed model on named consumer hardware, which is why hardware_relevance is deliberately left empty rather than padded with a datacenter id it does not use.
notes:
ADOPTION: in-production - open-sourced at Meta Connect 2024 (per the abstract) with released weights (open_weights true) and intended for resource-constrained deployment. VENUE NOTE: no peer-reviewed venue verifiable via Semantic Scholar and no arXiv comment venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Nov 2024). THE RECORD-LEVEL CONTRIBUTION IS THE COST ARITHMETIC, and it is the most quotable guardrail number in the repo: it establishes that a safety check can be had for 2.5s TTFT and 30 tok/s on a commodity mobile CPU at 440MB, which reframes 'guardrails are too expensive to run per-request' from a design constraint into an engineering tradeoff with a measured price. The 'comparable or superior' moderation claim is against the 1B non-quantised counterpart on safety scores - NOT against the 8B guard, and a reader who concludes int4 1B matches the 8B model would be over-reading. Two sizes are in play in the comparison and the record deliberately keeps them distinct.
